newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CBOE, OCC and Swiss bourse agree alliance.
newsitem.headline: CBOE, OCC and Swiss bourse agree alliance.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), the Options Clearing Corp (OCC) and the Swiss Bourse have signed a letter of intent to develop a common platform for trading and clearing derivative products, they said in a joint statement on Friday.
"It is expected that the project will be completed in the course of 1999," they said.

The OCC, the world's largest clearing house, is developing a new clearing platform whose software will be adapted to suit the needs of SOFFEX, the Swiss options and futures exchange that is a subsidiary of the Swiss Bourse.

"In a formal partnership, still to be established on the basis of the letter of intent, the three organisations also intend to license the common trading and clearing platform to third parties," they said.
In a first phase, the OCC will license its margining software for use in SOFFEX's clearing and the Swiss Bourse will license its SOFFEX trading software to the CBOE.
The CBOE and the Swiss Bourse will adapt the trading system for installation in Chicago to trade selected options and at Soffex for its members in Switzerland and Germany.

In a subsequent phase, the three partners will explore establishing a joint venture to develop a new trading system to be operated by the CBOE for disaster recovery purposes if needed. This might also be used to trade selected options. The Swiss Bourse could use it and the new clearing system for SOFFEX.
The letter of intent reflects a trend among futures and options exchanges to work more closely together.
The latest agreement emerged at the annual meeting in Buergenstock of the world's derivatives bourses.
